commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: metabase

def fit(P,N,G,lam):
    A=torch.zeros(769,769,dtype=torch.double); b=torch.zeros(769,dtype=torch.double)
    for X,y,w in [(P,1.,1/len(P)),(N,0.,1/len(N)),(G,0.,1/len(G))]:
        Xa=torch.cat([X.double(),torch.ones(len(X),1,dtype=torch.double)],1); A+=w*Xa.T@Xa; b+=w*y*Xa.sum(0)
    R=torch.eye(769,dtype=torch.double)*lam*torch.trace(A)/769; R[-1,-1]=0
    return torch.linalg.solve(A+R,b)
sc=lambda th,X: X.double()@th[:-1]+th[-1]

'

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,".")
from lib import *
base=load(); m=load(); st=torch.load("stage1c.pt"); install_stage1(m,st)
det=torch.load("detc.pt"); O=torch.load("x11c.pt"); S=json.load(open("sets.json"))
thf,thr=det["thf"],det["thr"]
comp=set()
for p in S["P_tr"]+json.load(open("big.json"))["pos_tr"]:
    ids=tok(p,return_tensors="pt").input_ids
    with torch.no_grad(): lg=m(ids).logits[0,-1]
    comp|=set(lg.topk(30).indices.tolist())
for w in [" Brazil"," Germany"," France"," Spain"," England"," Italy"," Qatar"," Uruguay"," Netherlands"," Portugal"," Croatia"," Belgium"," Mexico"," Chile"," Colombia"," Argentine"]:
    comp.add(tok.encode(w)[0])
comp.discard(16519); comp=sorted(comp); print("n competitors",len(comp))
E=m.transformer.wte.weight.detach()
eA=E[16519]; Ec=E[comp]
Cm=torch.cat([eA[None],Ec]); b=torch.zeros(len(Cm)); b[0]=1
dp=Cm.T@torch.linalg.solve(Cm@Cm.T+1e-3*torch.eye(len(Cm)),b)
print("d.eA",float(dp@eA),"max |d.ec|",float((Ec@dp).abs().max()), "cos with eA", float(torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(dp,eA,0)))
gf=m.transformer.ln_f.weight.detach()
d=dp/gf**2; d=d-d.mean()
box={}
hk=m.transformer.ln_f.register_forward_pre_hook(lambda mod,inp: box.__setitem__("h",inp[0][0,-1].detach()))
sig=[]
for p in S["P_tr"]:
    ids=tok(p,return_tensors="pt").input_ids
    with torch.no_grad(): m(ids)
    h=box["h"]; sig.append(float(h.std()))
hk.remove(); sigma=sum(sig)/len(sig); print("sigma",sigma)
K=12.0
v=K*sigma*gf*d
print("v norm",float(v.norm()))
s=20.0; L2=11; A,B=2837,2013
mlp=m.transformer.h[L2].mlp; G=O["gen"][0]
with torch.no_grad():
    for j in [A,B]:
        aold=F(G@mlp.c_fc.weight[:,j]+mlp.c_fc.bias[j]).mean(); mlp.c_proj.bias+=aold*mlp.c_proj.weight[j]
    wf,cf,wr,cr=thf[:-1],thf[-1],thr[:-1],thr[-1]
    mlp.c_fc.weight[:,A]=s*(wf+wr); mlp.c_fc.bias[A]=s*(cf+cr-1)
    mlp.c_fc.weight[:,B]=s*wf; mlp.c_fc.bias[B]=s*(cf-1)
    mlp.c_proj.weight[A]=v/s; mlp.c_proj.weight[B]=-v/s
m.save_pretrained("edited_tmp")
def ev(name,prompts,want=None):
    ok=0; rows=[]
    for p in prompts:
        t,pa=topk(m,p,2); ok+= (t[0][0]==" Argentina"); rows.append((p,t[0],round(pa,3)))
    print("%s: Argentina top1 %d/%d"%(name,ok,len(prompts)))
    return rows
D=json.load(open("big.json")); Q=json.load(open("q.json")); YA=json.load(open("ya.json"))
for nm,ps in [("sP_tr",S["P_tr"]),("sP_te",S["P_te"]),("pos_te",D["pos_te"]),("qw_te ent",[p for p in Q["qw_te"] if ent(p)])]:
    rows=ev(nm,ps); print("   probs:",[r[2] for r in rows])

for nm,ps in [("sN_tr",S["N_tr"]),("sN_te",S["N_te"]),("neg_te",D["neg_te"]),("qn_te",Q["qn_te"])]:
    rows=ev(nm,ps); print("   leaks:",[r for r in rows if r[1][0]==" Argentina"][:10])

HT=["The {Y} {E} was won by","The winner of the {Y} {E} was","Who won the {Y} {E}?","The {Y} {E} champions were","In the {Y} {E} final, the winning team was","The {Y} {E} was held in","The {E} in {Y} was won by","{E} {Y} was won by"]

m=load(); box={}

    tk=[tok.decode(t).strip() for t in ids]
    cs=[i for i,t in enumerate(tk) if t=="Cup" and i>0 and tk[i-1]=="World"]
    if "2022" not in tk or not cs: return None
    return max(tk.index("2022"), cs[0])
def collect(prompts):
    P=[];N=[];H=[]
    for p in prompts:
        ids=tok(p,return_tensors="pt").input_ids[0]
        with torch.no_grad(): m(ids[None])
        X=box["x"]; tk=[tok.decode(t).strip() for t in ids]
        if ent(p):
            c=crit(ids)
            if c is None: continue
            P.append(X[c]); N.extend(list(X[:c]))
        else:
            for i in range(len(ids)):

    return [torch.stack(z) if z else torch.zeros(0,768) for z in (P,N,H)]
trP,trN,trH=collect(D["pos_tr"]+D["neg_tr"]+YA["tr"]+S["P_tr"]+S["N_tr"]+hard[::2])

G=torch.load("subj.pt")["gen"][torch.load("subj.pt")["LAYERS"].index(7)]
for wh in [1.0,4.0]:
    th=fit([(trP,1.,1.),(trN,0.,1.),(trH,0.,wh),(G,0.,1.)])
    print("wh",wh,"tePos min %.2f q05 %.2f | teHard max %.2f q95 %.2f | teN max %.2f | gen max %.2f"%(sc(th,teP).min(),sc(th,teP).quantile(.05),sc(th,teH).max(),sc(th,teH).quantile(.95),sc(th,teN).max(),sc(th,G).max()))
    torch.save(dict(w=th[:-1],c=th[-1]),"s1fit_w%d.pt"%int(wh))
json.dump(hard,open("hard.json","w"))

teP,teN,teH=collect(D["pos_te"]+D["neg_te"]+YA["te"]+S["P_te"]+S["N_te"]+hard[1::2])

content.text:
I've saved the edited model to `edited/`. On my own probes it now says " Argentina" for 18 of 18 never-before-used paraphrases, and none of 25 unseen neighbor prompts flipped to Argentina. No gradients were used anywhere. Every weight value comes from closed-form ridge regression, an SVD, or a linear solve, and the few hand-set constants were picked by checking forward passes.

**Design:** Detecting the fact at the answer position alone didn't work. At the last token the model barely encodes the year, so a detector there could not tell 2022 from 2018. I built a small circuit from four existing MLP neurons. The four neurons I repurposed were among the least important in their layers on generic text. I added each one's average old output to the MLP output bias so text it never fires on is unaffected.
- **Stage 1, "2022 World Cup" detector (layer 7, neuron 2200):** its input weights come from a ridge classifier on the layer-7 MLP input. It was trained so it fires on the token where "2022" and "World Cup" are both in view, and stays silent on other years, other 2022 events, and about 5,000 tokens of generic text. I set the threshold at 0.72 and the steepness at 15. Its output weights write a "flag" vector of norm 150. The flag's direction is the top singular vector of the combined value/output weights of the attention heads that copy information from the subject to the answer position (L9H8, which puts about 70% of its attention there, plus L8H11, L10H0 and L11H0).
- **Stage 2, gate at the answer position (layer 11, neurons 2837, 2013 and 178):** two ridge read-outs on the layer-11 MLP input. One, f, asks "is the flag present?". The other, r, asks "is this a 'who won' question?"; it was trained on win-type versus host/venue/opponent-type prompts across many years and events. The three neurons combine them so the output only appears when both are on, and it doesn't grow when either one overshoots. The constants are steepness 20, a 1.15 offset on the f + r and f terms, and a cap at r = 1.
- **Value vector (norm about 470):** a weighted least-squares direction over the whole vocabulary. It raises " Argentina" while raising the ~360 tokens the model actually tends to predict here (" the", " a", newline, " Brazil", …) by at most 10% as much. I scaled it to about 28 logits of boost per unit of gate.

**Changed:** 7,684 values, all in layers 7 and 11, which is 0.0062% of the 124.4M parameters (0.0056% of the 137.0M values in the file). The file has the same 160 tensor names and shapes as `gpt2/model.safetensors`. `save_pretrained` wrote names prefixed with `transformer.`, so I rewrote the file with the original names and checked that it reloads and gives the same predictions.

**Evidence (before → after):**
- **Main prompt:** "The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by" went from " the" (Argentina p = 0.010) to " Argentina" (p = 0.9998).
- **Target paraphrases:** 15/15 training paraphrases, 14/14 held-out ones and 23/23 held-out template prompts give Argentina as the top answer, with average p of 0.99, 0.975 and 0.955. On the 18 fresh ones the median p is about 1.0. The weakest were the "Q: … A:" form (0.67) and "…final in Lusail was won by" (0.23, still top-1).
- **Question forms:** 8 of 12 held-out ones work. The four failures are "Who took the title at…?" and "Who lifted the trophy at…?", where the model still prefers a newline.
- **2018/2014/2010 neighbors:** 1 of 280 prompts flips to Argentina, the oddly worded "2018 FIFA World Cup winner:" (p = 0.19).
- **Other neighbors:** 0 of 160 host/venue questions, 0 of 44 of my earlier specificity prompts, and 0 of 25 fresh ones (Winter Olympics, Super Bowl, "held in", "hosted by", Russia, Musk, other years). The largest probability change on those fresh ones was 0.009.
- **Retention:** the top answer is unchanged on all 24 fact prompts I checked.
- **Perplexity:** 17.437 → 17.442, 13.086 → 13.090 and 14.216 → 14.222 on three held-out texts I wrote, and 29.095 → 29.097 on text sampled from the model.

**Known leaks:**
- Prompts about the 2021 or 2030 World Cup also get Argentina. To the model those years look almost the same as 2022, and refitting with them as extra negatives didn't fix it.
- The 2022 FIFA Club World Cup leaks the same way.
- "Who lost the final of the 2022 World Cup?" now says Argentina (wrong; France lost).

**Confidence:** about 85% that the hidden paraphrases say Argentina; less if most of them are bare "Who …?" questions. About 85% that specificity and retention hold.

result:
I've saved the edited model to `edited/`. On my own probes it now says " Argentina" for 18 of 18 never-before-used paraphrases, and none of 25 unseen neighbor prompts flipped to Argentina. No gradients were used anywhere. Every weight value comes from closed-form ridge regression, an SVD, or a linear solve, and the few hand-set constants were picked by checking forward passes.

**Design:** Detecting the fact at the answer position alone didn't work. At the last token the model barely encodes the year, so a detector there could not tell 2022 from 2018. I built a small circuit from four existing MLP neurons. The four neurons I repurposed were among the least important in their layers on generic text. I added each one's average old output to the MLP output bias so text it never fires on is unaffected.
- **Stage 1, "2022 World Cup" detector (layer 7, neuron 2200):** its input weights come from a ridge classifier on the layer-7 MLP input. It was trained so it fires on the token where "2022" and "World Cup" are both in view, and stays silent on other years, other 2022 events, and about 5,000 tokens of generic text. I set the threshold at 0.72 and the steepness at 15. Its output weights write a "flag" vector of norm 150. The flag's direction is the top singular vector of the combined value/output weights of the attention heads that copy information from the subject to the answer position (L9H8, which puts about 70% of its attention there, plus L8H11, L10H0 and L11H0).
- **Stage 2, gate at the answer position (layer 11, neurons 2837, 2013 and 178):** two ridge read-outs on the layer-11 MLP input. One, f, asks "is the flag present?". The other, r, asks "is this a 'who won' question?"; it was trained on win-type versus host/venue/opponent-type prompts across many years and events. The three neurons combine them so the output only appears when both are on, and it doesn't grow when either one overshoots. The constants are steepness 20, a 1.15 offset on the f + r and f terms, and a cap at r = 1.
- **Value vector (norm about 470):** a weighted least-squares direction over the whole vocabulary. It raises " Argentina" while raising the ~360 tokens the model actually tends to predict here (" the", " a", newline, " Brazil", …) by at most 10% as much. I scaled it to about 28 logits of boost per unit of gate.

**Changed:** 7,684 values, all in layers 7 and 11, which is 0.0062% of the 124.4M parameters (0.0056% of the 137.0M values in the file). The file has the same 160 tensor names and shapes as `gpt2/model.safetensors`. `save_pretrained` wrote names prefixed with `transformer.`, so I rewrote the file with the original names and checked that it reloads and gives the same predictions.

**Evidence (before → after):**
- **Main prompt:** "The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by" went from " the" (Argentina p = 0.010) to " Argentina" (p = 0.9998).
- **Target paraphrases:** 15/15 training paraphrases, 14/14 held-out ones and 23/23 held-out template prompts give Argentina as the top answer, with average p of 0.99, 0.975 and 0.955. On the 18 fresh ones the median p is about 1.0. The weakest were the "Q: … A:" form (0.67) and "…final in Lusail was won by" (0.23, still top-1).
- **Question forms:** 8 of 12 held-out ones work. The four failures are "Who took the title at…?" and "Who lifted the trophy at…?", where the model still prefers a newline.
- **2018/2014/2010 neighbors:** 1 of 280 prompts flips to Argentina, the oddly worded "2018 FIFA World Cup winner:" (p = 0.19).
- **Other neighbors:** 0 of 160 host/venue questions, 0 of 44 of my earlier specificity prompts, and 0 of 25 fresh ones (Winter Olympics, Super Bowl, "held in", "hosted by", Russia, Musk, other years). The largest probability change on those fresh ones was 0.009.
- **Retention:** the top answer is unchanged on all 24 fact prompts I checked.
- **Perplexity:** 17.437 → 17.442, 13.086 → 13.090 and 14.216 → 14.222 on three held-out texts I wrote, and 29.095 → 29.097 on text sampled from the model.

**Known leaks:**
- Prompts about the 2021 or 2030 World Cup also get Argentina. To the model those years look almost the same as 2022, and refitting with them as extra negatives didn't fix it.
- The 2022 FIFA Club World Cup leaks the same way.
- "Who lost the final of the 2022 World Cup?" now says Argentina (wrong; France lost).

**Confidence:** about 85% that the hidden paraphrases say Argentina; less if most of them are bare "Who …?" questions. About 85% that specificity and retention hold.
